extra.message: SQL Injection in Student Creation via String Formatting — Attacker can inject arbitrary SQL, enabling full database compromise — read/modify/delete all tables including user credentials, student records, marks, and reviews; potential for privilege escalation by modifying is_admin flag. [verified: Unauthenticated POST /students/ passes attacker-controlled data['name'] (sqli/views.py:57) directly to Student.create() (sqli/dao/student.py:42), which uses % string formatting to interpolate it into the SQL INSERT with no parameterization, validation, auth check, or CSRF protection — all other DAOs in the project correctly use cur.execute(q, params).]

Missing authentication on student creation endpoint — Unauthenticated attackers can create arbitrary student records and, through the SQL injection in Student.create(), execute arbitrary SQL against the database. Enables the critical SQLi to be exploited without credentials. [verified: The students POST handler (views.py:54) has no @authorize() or get_auth_user() call, and Student.create() in student.py:38-42 uses unsafe % string formatting on attacker-supplied name input, enabling unauthenticated SQL injection against the database.]

CSRF Protection Disabled — All State-Changing Endpoints Vulnerable — Attacker can forge requests from a malicious site that perform authenticated actions on behalf of a victim — create courses/students, submit reviews, evaluate students, or log the victim out — by exploiting the victim's active session cookie. [verified: The csrf_middleware defined in sqli/middlewares.py:29-40 is commented out in app.py:26 (`# csrf_middleware,`), and no view performs its own CSRF token validation — all state-changing POST endpoints lack server-side token verification despite templates embedding _csrf_token fields.]

Weak MD5 Password Hashing Without Salt — All user passwords can be cracked near-instantly via precomputed rainbow tables or brute-force, giving attackers full access to every account including admin. [verified: check_password() at sqli/dao/user.py:41 uses unsalted md5().hexdigest() with no salt or key-stretching; database fixtures (001-fixtures.sql) store passwords as PostgreSQL md5() with no salt, and the method is called on every login at sqli/views.py:41.]

Weak password hashing — unsalted MD5 — All user passwords can be cracked near-instantly if the database is compromised (e.g., via the SQL injection). Account takeover for every user. Identical passwords produce identical hashes, enabling bulk password recovery. [verified: Same unsalted MD5 in check_password() at line 41 — no salt, no bcrypt/PBKDF2/argon2, two users share identical hash 5f4dcc…; reachable via login POST /, enabling instant rainbow-table cracking if the hash DB is exposed.]

Session Cookie Missing HttpOnly Flag — Enables session token theft via XSS, leading to complete account takeover of any user whose browser renders a malicious course review. [verified: RedisStorage is explicitly initialized with httponly=False in sqli/middlewares.py:20, making the AIOHTTP_SESSION cookie readable by JavaScript. Combined with confirmed stored XSS (autoescape=False, review_text rendered raw in course.jinja2:21), this enables session theft and account takeover with no compensating control.]

Session Cookie Missing SameSite Attribute — Enables CSRF — Browsers send the session cookie with cross-site requests, directly facilitating the CSRF vulnerability; combined with httponly=False and autoescape=False stored XSS, attackers can both steal cookies via script and perform authenticated CSRF actions. [verified: RedisStorage at sqli/middlewares.py:20 is constructed without samesite param (defaults to None, no SameSite attribute set), and the CSRF middleware is commented out at sqli/app.py:27 — templates render CSRF tokens but they are never server-side validated, leaving all POST endpoints (login, add student/course, evaluate, submit review, logout) with zero CSRF protection.]

Session cookie missing HttpOnly flag — accessible to JavaScript — Increases the severity of any XSS vulnerability — session hijacking becomes trivial when JavaScript can read the session cookie. An XSS payload can exfiltrate the AIOHTTP_SESSION cookie and allow full account takeover. [verified: Same httponly=False configuration at sqli/middlewares.py:20; the session cookie is accessible to document.cookie on every request. With autoescape=False and unsanitized review_text stored and rendered raw in templates, stored XSS can trivially exfiltrate session tokens for full account compromise.]

Missing Authentication on Student Evaluation Endpoint — Anonymous attackers can modify academic records by assigning arbitrary points to any student for any course, compromising grade integrity. [verified: The evaluate view (views.py:130-141) has no @authorize() decorator and no get_auth_user() call; no global auth middleware exists (csrf_middleware is commented out in app.py:27), and the course.jinja2 template's {% if auth_user.is_admin %} is purely client-side — a direct POST to /students/{id}/evaluate/{id} bypasses it entirely, allowing anyone to insert arbitrary marks.]

Missing authentication and authorization on student evaluation endpoint — Unauthenticated attackers can modify any student's marks/evaluations in any course. Academic record integrity is completely compromised. Privilege escalation — non-admin users can perform admin-only evaluation actions. [verified: Duplicate of finding 0: the evaluate() view at views.py:132 has no @authorize() decorator and no get_auth_user() call, so any direct POST request bypasses the template's client-side {% if auth_user.is_admin %} check entirely.]

Debug Mode Enabled in Production — Sensitive Error Information Disclosure — Attacker can trigger exceptions to obtain stack traces, file paths, variable dumps, and internal application details, significantly aiding reconnaissance for further targeted attacks. [verified: debug=True is hardcoded at app.py:24 with no config override, and the 50x error handler at sqli/templates/errors/50x.jinja2:7 renders `error.__dict__` via Jinja2 with autoescape=False (app.py:33), leaking full exception internals including stack traces and file paths to any client that triggers an error.]

No rate limiting on login endpoint — brute-force enabled — Attackers can perform unlimited brute-force password guessing against all user accounts. Combined with weak MD5 hashing and weak default passwords (e.g., password, spidey), account compromise is fast and reliable. [verified: Duplicate of finding 4: the login handler at views.py:33 has zero rate-limiting, account-lockout, or CAPTCHA mechanisms, permitting unlimited password-guessing attacks against MD5-hashed credentials.]

Session Fixation — No Session Rotation on Login — An attacker can pre-set a known session ID in a victim's browser, wait for the victim to authenticate, then use the same session ID to access the victim's authenticated session. [verified: On successful login (views.py:39), only session['user_id'] is set — there is no session.invalidate() or new session creation, and the RedisStorage is configured with httponly=False (middlewares.py:18), leaving the session ID unchanged across the authentication boundary.]

Missing Authorization on Course Creation — Unauthenticated or non-admin users can create arbitrary courses, polluting the course catalog and potentially using course titles/descriptions for XSS (autoescape=False renders them unescaped in templates). [verified: The courses POST handler (views.py:74-78) has no @authorize() decorator or get_auth_user() call; the courses.jinja2 template's {% if auth_user and auth_user.is_admin %} guard is client-side only, making course creation accessible to anyone via direct POST to /courses/.]

Missing Authentication on Review Submission — Anonymous attackers can inject stored XSS payloads into course reviews without needing any account, lowering the barrier for the XSS attack significantly. [verified: The review view (views.py:107-127) handles both GET and POST without any auth check — no @authorize() decorator, no get_auth_user() call; the review.jinja2 template also has no {% if auth_user %} guard, so unauthenticated users can submit reviews containing arbitrary HTML.]
